topComment.author: @bzdirt
topComment.text:
Reminds me of the time we worked on Gangstar. The team had to fit a "GTA-like" on the first iPhone. I think it was the first 3D open-world on iPhone. The challenge wasn't as much the memory as it was the rendering.
We actually use some tricks similar to GTA: if you had a car, others would be those using the same atlas of textures (so they could be batched together). The view frustum would be super aggressive so stuff would depop behind so it could pop in front of you. No flight so there could be islands of void in some areas. And the most important: no straight roads. Not for long anyway. That wasn't because of speed but because we wanted to make the city feel larger, and make it so you couldn't see too far ahead. And so if you go in a straight line and take the most obvious turn, you pass through pretty much every road out there, rather than driving in circle on the same street again and again.
And since we really couldn't display much ahead, we made one big imposter city (atrociously low-res) drawn behind the real one. As for streaming? No time to make such tech, so it was just one very long loading at the start of the game!

@ak-ub1ym ​They can now too. It’s not a matter of ability to, they just don’t need button codes to do tests quickly nowadays.

There’s also modern considerations that didn’t exist back then, like online integrated aspects, achievements, and way more game that are competitive oriented than back in the day, that you have to take into consideration when allowing gameplay cheats and causes devs to just not bother with them for the extra workload they bring (especially with all extra debugging they require because of this). Plus, publishers have realizee that when you do have features that used to be behind cheat codes, it’s better to sell them as DLC than to just give them away for free. topComment.author: @TimRomero
topComment.text: 8:03 often wall squeezes are used for non streaming reasons. They let you out in a fixed exact location which makes it easy to transition seamlessly into a cinematic without moving the player as we see in this TLOU example. They also can be used as a “blood gate” to lock you into completing combat encounters by disallowing you from using the interact until you’re out of combat.

replies.author: @fabiangiesen306
replies.text:
This! Or just as one-way doors in a game with a linear level design to prevent a player from backtracking too much if they get turned around for whatever reason.

A major tell for actual technical constraints being the reason is everyone's favorite, the S-bend corridor (too many games to mention) or big rooms where all exits lead to tiny rooms (e.g. the Metroid Prime series). The former breaks line of sight so either room connected to it can see into the corridor but not past it, the latter has to do with how that series' memory management works (the game always keeps the current room and at most one other connected room in memory, so all possible pairs of connected rooms have to fit in the streaming pool).

I remember noticing memory tricks in a couple of GameCube games:

Wind Waker appears to work on a sector-by-sector basis - the Great Sea is divided into a 7x7 grid, with the current grid square fully loaded, and a buffer zone around the borders - a minimum distance from the sector boundary that any island has to be. Meanwhile, major islands are visible from a lot further away - at the time, I concluded they were painted on the skybox for each sector, but I forget whether I considered the possibility that they were 2D billboards instead - either way, I remember seeing the details of a distant major island visibly change as I crossed the boundary between grid squares.

In Metroid Prime, the streaming doesn't always keep up - if you shoot a door to open it, the game waits until the room beyond has fully loaded before opening the door, and you can end up with a second or two waiting before the door opens - which is a lot when you've just dodged and weaved across an entire room full of enemies to reach the door, planning to dive through and let it close behind you - suddenly, you're having to evade attacks coming from behind while you wait...
